children: The insurer settles over 85,900 cancer-related claims, highlighting the growing importance of early detection, treatment access and financial protection for women

Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited settled more than 85,900 cancer-related claims worth over Rs 780 crore during the first half of FY2026-27, with women accounting for nearly 60 per cent of the payouts, the company announced on 5 November, 2026. Settlements for women increased 17 per cent year-on-year, while nearly 30 per cent of the total claims were associated with people aged between 51 and 60 years.

According to the insurer, more than 45 per cent of the cancer claim payouts originated from Maharashtra, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The figures highlight the financial support required by patients and families navigating cancer treatment.

A 2013 study published in the Asian Pacific Journal of Cancer Prevention, based on Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) National Cancer Registry Programme data from 2001-2004, projected approximately 9.35 lakh new cancer cases among women in India for 2026. Breast and cervical cancers were identified among the leading contributors. The figure represents a projection rather than an observed 2026 count.

Government screening initiatives have also expanded. By February 2026, approximately 8.73 crore women had been screened for cervical cancer under the national programme for prevention and control of non-communicable diseases, with 93,062 diagnoses reported.

Star Health said it conducted community health camps during H1 FY27, including initiatives focused on cancer screening and preventive healthcare, to improve awareness and encourage engagement with healthcare services.

Amitabh Jain, Whole-time Director and Chief Operating Officer, Star Health and Allied Insurance, said early detection must be accompanied by access to treatment and financial protection. He emphasised that financial preparedness should support the treatment journey rather than remain an afterthought following diagnosis.

Prof. Dr S. Rajasundaram, Surgical Oncologist, said cancer treatment often involves multiple stages, including chemotherapy, radiation, surgery and long-term monitoring. Financial constraints can lead families to postpone or discontinue treatment, potentially affecting clinical outcomes.

He highlighted health insurance as an important financial cushion that can help families access prescribed treatments and maintain continuity of care. The company said its focus remains on strengthening financial protection and encouraging preventive healthcare awareness, particularly among women.
